Run the four tests of the identification assumptions

Source: R/rd_checks.R
rd_checks.Rd

When the running variable moves over time, the estimate of didisc() is identified under type continuity, constant within-type confounding, and either composition stability or homogeneous confounding (Leventer and Nevo, 2024). rd_checks() runs the four tests, rd_typecont(), rd_compstable(), rd_homog() and rd_trendcell(), with one set of options, and prints one table. Each test's own result is kept, so every detail stays available.

Usage

rd_checks(
  data,
  y,
  x,
  time,
  id,
  t_rd,
  comparisons = NULL,
  estimand = c("att", "atu"),
  c = 0,
  kernel = "triangular",
  scheme = c("auto", "cs", "pc", "pv"),
  bc = TRUE,
  joint = c("supt", "swald", "wald"),
  studentize = TRUE,
  outcome_bwselect = c("pooled", "cct", "rot"),
  typecont = list(),
  compstable = list(),
  homog = list(),
  trendcell = list(),
  level = 0.95
)

Arguments

data, y, x, time, id

as in didisc(); id is required.

t_rd

the RD period (required).

comparisons, estimand, c, kernel, scheme, bc

shared by the four tests; defaults as in each test.

joint

the joint statistic of rd_typecont() and rd_compstable(): "supt" (default), "swald" or "wald" (the chi-squared Wald).

studentize

for joint = "supt" or "swald": TRUE (default; t critical values) or FALSE (normal critical values).

outcome_bwselect

the bandwidth rule of rd_homog() and rd_trendcell(): "pooled" (default; one bandwidth for every cell, the CCT bandwidth of the outcome on the pooled comparison periods), "cct" (one CCT bandwidth per cell) or "rot" (a rule of thumb per cell). The share tests' own bwselect (per-fit CCT by default) can be changed in typecont / compstable; their rule of thumb is a different one (0.5 * IQR(x) in every regression).

typecont, compstable, homog, trendcell

lists of further arguments for one test, which override the shared ones.

level

the confidence level of the reading in the printout (default 0.95, as in didisc()): a test rejects when its p-value is below 1 - level.

Value

An object of class "rd_checks": a list with table (one row per test: test, assumption, statistic, p_value, method, bandwidth, error), the four test results typecont, compstable, homog, trendcell (NULL where a test failed), level and call.

Details

The arguments shared by the four tests (t_rd, comparisons, estimand, c, kernel, scheme, bc) are set once. joint and studentize apply to the two tests on type shares, outcome_bwselect to the two tests on the outcome; see the help of each test for what they do. Anything else, or a different value for one test only, goes in that test's list, for example typecont = list(joint = "wald") or homog = list(bwselect = "cct", min_n = 20). A test that cannot run on the data (for example, no unit changes side of the cutoff) gives a row with its error message and NA results.

The printout ends with a reading at the confidence level level, as in didisc(): a test rejects its assumption when its p-value is below 1 - level. Not rejecting an assumption does not establish it; constant within-type confounding concerns the RD period and is checked in the comparison periods only (a pre-trends check).

See also

rd_typecont(), rd_compstable(), rd_homog(), rd_trendcell(); tidy() in didisc-tidiers.

Other tests of the assumptions: plot.rd_compstable(), plot.rd_homog(), plot.rd_trendcell(), plot.rd_typecont(), plot_switchers(), rd_compstable(), rd_homog(), rd_trendcell(), rd_typecont()

Examples

ch <- rd_checks(didisc_sim_pv, y = "Y", x = "R", time = "year", id = "id", t_rd = 3)
ch
#> Tests of the identification assumptions  [rd_checks()]
#> 
#>   Assumption                          Statistic        p   Statistic type             Bandwidth
#>   type continuity                         1.232    0.869   sup-t, t critical values   CCT per cell
#>   composition stability                   3.086    0.016   sup-t, t critical values   CCT per cell
#>   homogeneous confounding                 0.247    0.884   Wald chi-squared(2)        pooled CCT, h = 0.21
#>   constant within-type confounding        1.445    0.485   Wald chi-squared(2)        pooled CCT, h = 0.21
#> 
#>   Reading at level 0.95, rejecting when p < 0.05 (not rejecting does not establish an assumption):
#>     type continuity                    not rejected
#>     composition stability              rejected     } identification needs
#>     homogeneous confounding            not rejected } only one of these two
#>     constant within-type confounding   not rejected (checked in the comparison periods)
#>   Each test's details: x$typecont, x$compstable, x$homog, x$trendcell.
# switch options: the chi-squared Wald and per-cell bandwidths everywhere
rd_checks(didisc_sim_pv, y = "Y", x = "R", time = "year", id = "id", t_rd = 3,
          joint = "wald", outcome_bwselect = "cct")
#> Tests of the identification assumptions  [rd_checks()]
#> 
#>   Assumption                          Statistic        p   Statistic type             Bandwidth
#>   type continuity                         4.782    0.853   Wald chi-squared(9)        CCT per cell
#>   composition stability                  23.647   <0.001   Wald chi-squared(6)        CCT per cell
#>   homogeneous confounding                 0.465    0.793   Wald chi-squared(2)        CCT per cell
#>   constant within-type confounding        0.078    0.962   Wald chi-squared(2)        CCT per cell
#> 
#>   Reading at level 0.95, rejecting when p < 0.05 (not rejecting does not establish an assumption):
#>     type continuity                    not rejected
#>     composition stability              rejected     } identification needs
#>     homogeneous confounding            not rejected } only one of these two
#>     constant within-type confounding   not rejected (checked in the comparison periods)
#>   Each test's details: x$typecont, x$compstable, x$homog, x$trendcell.
